vera_rubin_kent_ford_1970s_measured_ho: Rubin, Ford and other observers established extended rotation curves for spiral galaxies. A compact central mass gives circular speed proportional to r⁻¹ᐟ² far outside it. A galaxy has distributed stars and gas, so its expected curve must use their spatial mass profiles. Many measured outer speeds exceed the Newtonian stars-and-gas contribution for plausible stellar masses. Rotation curves constrain the gravitational field; interpreting the difference as a dark halo depends on the mass model and gravity assumptions.
about_5_of_the_universe_is_ordinary_ma: In the Planck 2018 base ΛCDM interpretation, the present-day cosmic energy budget is approximately 5% ordinary matter, 27% dark matter and 68% dark energy. These are inferred cosmological density fractions. They describe today’s universe; they are not the mixture at recombination or the mass fractions of an individual galaxy.
the_cosmic_microwave_background_has_ti: The CMB temperature and polarization patterns contain acoustic peaks. Cosmological models connect those patterns to baryon density, dark-matter density, geometry and other parameters. Planck’s base ΛCDM analysis infers a present-day budget of roughly 5% ordinary matter, 27% dark matter and 68% dark energy. The inference uses a model of cosmic evolution; the CMB does not directly observe that present-day mixture.
rot_difference_title: Observed speed minus the stars and gas model, with quoted measurement errors
rot_chart_title: SPARC measured rotation speeds with error bars and an adjustable stars and gas model
rot_above: Observed speed is above the stars and gas model
rot_below: The stars and gas model is above the observed speed
rot_overlap: The model lies within the quoted speed error bar
rot_undefined: This mass choice gives no circular-speed solution
rot_intro: Compare published SPARC speeds with the Newtonian contribution from stars and gas. Choose a galaxy, change the assumed stellar mass per unit light, and inspect a measured radius. The observations stay fixed.
rot_ml_help: Higher M/L assigns more stellar mass to the same light. Stellar speed contributions scale with √(M/L). The 0.5 example follows a reference choice in SPARC; this control explores an assumption.
rot_radius_help: Drag the radius slider or speed chart. Selection snaps to a published sample. Arrow keys move one sample; Shift moves five. Home selects the innermost sample and End selects the outermost. One kiloparsec (kpc) is about 3,260 light-years.
rot_observed_key: White points and bars: published speeds and quoted errors.
rot_model_key: Gold dashed: stars and gas model at this M/L.
rot_chart_caption: Both examples use the same speed scale. Straight model segments join the tabulated radii. The curve contains no fitted dark halo.
rot_difference_caption: Difference = observed speed − stars and gas speed. Zero means equal speeds. Positive values put the observed speed above the model; negative values retain an overprediction. Bars carry the quoted speed errors only. Model uncertainty is not included.
rot_status_scope: This comparison uses the listed random error at one radius. It is not a statistical fit or a dark-matter detection. Interpreting a gap needs assumptions about gravity, distance, inclination and the stellar population.
rot_data_source: SPARC (Lelli, McGaugh & Schombert, 2016), Tables 1 and 2. NGC 3198 and NGC 6503 are shown at the published distances and inclinations. The quoted speed errors describe random non-circular motions and kinematic asymmetries; they exclude inclination systematics.
rot_equation: The Newtonian model adds squared speed contributions: v² = Vgas|Vgas| + (M/L)Vdisk|Vdisk| + (M/L)Vbulge|Vbulge|. SPARC tabulates stellar terms at M/L = 1. These two examples have zero bulge terms. The signed gas term preserves an outward force from central gas depressions.
rot_model_limits: Gas terms include the catalog’s factor 1.33 for helium. The model keeps gas, light profiles, adopted distance and inclination fixed. It does not fit a halo, compute a joint likelihood, infer a particle type or model modified gravity. The numerical data are bundled for offline use.
rot_original_sources: Original rotation-curve references listed by SPARC: NGC 3198 — Daigle et al. (2006), Begeman et al. (1991), Begeman (1987); NGC 6503 — Begeman et al. (1991), Begeman (1987).
